name: execveat
synopsis: int execveat(int dirfd, const char *pathname, char *const argv[], char *const envp[], int flags);
description: The execveat() system call executes a program relative to a directory file descriptor. It operates like execve(2) but allows interpreting relative paths based on the specified file descriptor.

parameters.name: dirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor, or AT_FDCWD to use the current working directory

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.description: Path to the executable; relative paths are resolved relative to dirfd

parameters.name: argv
parameters.description: Array of argument strings for the new program

parameters.name: envp
parameters.description: Array of environment variable strings for the new program

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Bit mask of flags, such as AT_EMPTY_PATH or AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: flags includes AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW and the file is a symbolic link
Program requires an interpreter but dirfd was opened with O_CLOEXEC, making it inaccessible
pathname is relative and dirfd is not a directory

bugs: It is not possible to set the close-on-exec flag on the file descriptor for calls with an empty pathname and AT_EMPTY_PATH, leading to file descriptor leaks and potential exhaustion in recursive scenarios.
